source_text: Thales Milesius unus e septem sapientibus, deinde Anaximander, Anaximenes, Anaxagoras, Xenophanes, Parmenides, Leucippus, Democritus, Empedocles, Heraclitus, Melissus, Plato, Pythagoraei Omnes philosophi in scholis licet aliud disserentes, tamen idola cum plebe venerantes, qui de naturalibus causis aliquid excogitare conati sunt, inter multas opinionis suae vanitates, aliquas tamen veritatis velut lambere partes, qui per caliginem vani, huic tamen dogmati contra quod xagimus, iure anteferri possunt omnes philosophos, qui de naturalibus causis aliquid excogitare conati sunt, iureposse huic dogmati, contra quod ageres, anteferri
pass_a_gloss: Thales Milesius one from seven sapientibus, then Anaximander, Anaximenes, Anaxagoras, Xenophanes, Parmenides, Leucippus, Democritus, Empedocles, Heraclitus, Melissus, Plato, Pythagoraei all philosophi in scholis although other disserentes, nevertheless idola when/with plebe venerantes, who about/from naturalibus causis something excogitare conati are, among multas opinionis his-own vanitates, aliquas nevertheless of-truth as-if lambere partes, who through caliginem vani, to-this nevertheless dogmati against that/which xagimus, by-right anteferri are-able all philosophos, who about/from naturalibus causis something excogitare conati are, iureposse to-this dogmati, against that/which ageres, anteferri.
pass_b_english: All the philosophers who tried to work out anything about the causes of natural things—even though they taught otherwise in their schools yet worshiped idols with the common people—have nevertheless touched, as it were, some parts of truth amid the many empty notions in their thinking. Empty though they are through their darkness, they can rightly be preferred to this doctrine we are opposing.
Thales of Miletus, one of the Seven Sages; then Anaximander, Anaximenes, Anaxagoras, Xenophanes, Parmenides, Leucippus, Democritus, Empedocles, Heraclitus, Melissus, Plato, and the Pythagoreans.

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
